sources.note: Official degree requirements 2026-27: Professional Master's in Global Affairs, 28 credits
Curriculum: core, electives, capstone, Deep Dive trips; electives not tied to a track
Admissions: any undergraduate field of study accepted

subject_rule: Open to any undergraduate field of study: the programme states there is no requirement for a specific field and all fields are welcome. The scholarship funds one single programme, the Professional Master's in Global Affairs at Schwarzman College, with no majors or concentrations.

programmes.name: Professional Master's in Global Affairs
programmes.detail: One-year programme in Beijing taught in English; 28 degree credits in 4 modules (core 11 credits, electives at least 6, professional ethics 1, language 2, Deep Dive 2, Capstone Project 3, orientation 1, Practice in Global Leadership 2); no majors or concentrations, electives need not be focused in one area

notes: Master's: 1 programme recorded; it is the only programme the scholarship funds, so this is the full official list.

The programme has no majors, tracks or concentrations. The curriculum page says students are not required to focus their electives in any one area. The three themed Deep Dive in China field-trip types (Business Development, State-led Development, Rural Development) are trip themes inside a two-credit course, not degree tracks, so they are not recorded as programmes.

Core course groups named on the curriculum page: Global Affairs, China, Leadership Core, Leadership in Practice, Professional Ethics; electives are China-focused and additional electives drawn mainly from public policy, economics and business, and international studies, and Scholars may take courses from other English-taught Tsinghua master's programmes (law, public health, public policy, international relations, environmental studies, business, education).
The curriculum page's course lists were shown only in part (a Load more button); individual courses are not recorded as they are courses, not majors.
Degree requirements are for academic year 2026-27; the Class of 2028-2029 requirements may change.
not_stated: The admissions page does not name the degree title; the degree requirements document names it the Professional Master's in Global Affairs.
